newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends mixed, Nov/Jan switch eases.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends mixed, Nov/Jan switch eases.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures closed tightly mixed in a quiet, shortened afternoon session ahead of a U.K. trade dinner in London on Friday.

Conditions were thin as the market closed an hour earlier ahead of the annual get-together. Traders said the only prominent market feature was the weakening of the November/January switch on trade selling.
The Nov/Jan spread traded at $46, down from $52 at Thursday's close and a high of $90 seen earlier in the week.
Traders said the November premium to January was being eroded by liquidation as funds rolled their short positions into the back months and fueled by perception of rising U.K. certified stocks.
The U.K. September certified stock data, due to be released on Tuesday, are expected to show a slight rise to over 1,000 five-tonne lots from August's 929 lots, traders said.
"Because it (the stock) is going to go up, that's why you see people liquidate their few positions on November in London," one said.
By the finish, November was down $3 at $1,520 a tonne after a high of $1,537.
Traders said values were mainly depressed by persistent Asian and African producer selling, outweighing slight gains on arbitrage buying against New York.
On the fundamental front, traders said the current tight supplies of nearby physical coffee remained the main talking point especially in the United States market.
U.S. roaster Maxwell House, a division of Kraft Foods, on Thursday denied market talk that it was having to close a plant due to a shortage of coffee.
Instead the firm had temporarily halted output for about a week for maintenance.
One trader said there was also persistent talk of a Peruvian default of 10,000 to 14,000 60-kg bags to a U.S. warehouse in Jacksonville.
